section_summary: This final section closes a Japanese political address advocating a return to economic freedom, repudiation of politicians associated with the Tojo cabinet, parliamentary liberalism, fair play, and women’s political participation. It is followed by an English contents sheet for the Japan Liberal Party’s November 1945 emergency policies and a Japanese checklist concerning election administration, candidate deposits, notices, and related procedures.

people.name: Hideki Tojo
people.role: Former prime minister; his cabinet and its political collaborators are condemned in the address.

people.name: Philip Snowden
people.role: Chancellor of the Exchequer in Britain’s first Labour government, cited as an example of a politician whose speech was praised by opponents.
variants: フイリツプスノーテン

subfiles.title: Political address on liberalism, political responsibility, and women’s suffrage
subfiles.to: Japanese electorate, especially prospective women voters
subfiles.about: The speaker outlines a liberal program for Japan’s economic and political reconstruction and urges women to exercise their newly granted voting rights.
subfiles.summary: A party address calling for an end to the controlled economy, accountability for politicians who backed the Tojo cabinet, liberalism, and women's suffrage amid food unrest and communist appeals.

subfiles.title: Emergency Policies of Japan Liberal Party
subfiles.about: An English-language contents sheet lists the principal subject divisions of the party’s emergency policy program.
subfiles.summary: Contents outline of the Japan Liberal Party's emergency policies by subject, from foreign policy and finance to labor, women and war criminals.

subfiles.title: 選舉事務ニ關スル事項 (Matters concerning election administration)
subfiles.about: Brief Japanese notes enumerate procedural matters relating to elections, including records, observers, candidate deposits, notices, and deadlines.
subfiles.summary: Election administration checklist covering account books, observers, candidate deposits of 2,000 yen, deadlines, and voter qualifications.
